items.text: Markets: Half-day Black Friday, and Wall Street came back from turkey break swinging. Futures had the Nasdaq 100 up about 2.3%, the S&P 500 about 1.6%, and the Dow about 1.4% into the open as dip buyers piled back into AI stocks. Bell rings early at 1 p.m. ET. The kicker? The S&P and Nasdaq are still on pace for their worst November since 2008.

Markets: Bitcoin is up about 1.8% to around $61,600 and on track to snap a seven-week losing streak if it holds through Sunday. Still down about 20% for November, and the Fear & Greed index sits at 11. Extreme fear, but make it festive.

What's New: A president demanding an investigation because the economy grew FASTER than reported. Q3 GDP got revised up to 4.3% from 3.4%, and Trump called it a "RECORD SETTING ERROR." CNBC checked: tied for 16th since 1990. Not a record.

Leveling Up: Thanksgiving football, period. Bears won with 3 seconds left, Eagles with 2 seconds left, Bills as time expired. Per Elias, it's the first day in NFL history where every game had a go-ahead score in the final minute.
Leveling Up: Joe Milton III, revenge arc unlocked. He walked into Jerry's World and beat his former team. The Eagles were down 31-10 and won 39-38, the biggest Thanksgiving comeback in NFL history.

Took a Hit: Harrison Butker's kicking. He missed a go-ahead 46-yarder in a 10-10 game, then watched Tyler Bass drill a 57-yarder at the buzzer. Butker is 15-for-23 this year, most misses in the league, and Andy Reid won't say if he's still the kicker.

Still Broken: The lights. Nearly 670,000 customers were still without power Friday morning after the Thanksgiving nor'easter, down from about 1 million Thursday night. Pennsylvania, New Jersey and Maryland got hit worst, and Baltimore's utility says it's "looking like a couple days."

Leveling Up: Central Park's rain gauge. 2.18 inches on Thanksgiving, smashing the Nov. 26 record of 1.91 inches from 1996. That's nearly 17 times a normal day. Your gravy boat was not the only thing overflowing.

Happening Now: The parade side quest. The 100th Macy's parade steps off Saturday at 8:30 a.m., and the bands are scrambling. A Texas high school band raised $350,000 in hours to stay, Hawaii's band needed about $700,000, and Alabama's Million Dollar Band went home to play the Iron Bowl.

What's New: Old-school Black Friday respawned in Frisco, Texas. Hundreds lined up outside JCPenney before 5 a.m., and the store set up an inflatable cash cube giving shoppers 30 seconds to grab as many bills as they could for gift cards. 2009 called.
